question.prompt: Box A contains 2 red balls and 1 white ball, and box B contains 1 red ball and 2 white balls. First, a box is chosen with equal probability, and then 1 ball is drawn from that box. What is the probability of drawing a red ball?

solutions.explanation: The probability of choosing box A and then drawing red is \(1/3\), and the probability of choosing box B and then drawing red is \(1/6\). Adding gives \(1/2\).
solutions.title: Add the two box paths

solutions.explanation: Assume each ball in the selected box is equally likely to be drawn. Because the boxes are chosen with equal probability and each contains 3 balls, all 6 individual balls have the same chance of being drawn. Each ball belongs to exactly one box, so counting them covers every possible draw once. There are \(2+1=3\) red balls among these 6 balls. Thus the probability of red is \(3/6=1/2\).
solutions.title: Recognize six equally likely balls
